caveats.tlds: A country-code TLD is a DNS delegation, not a jurisdiction: many ccTLDs are registered worldwide (e.g. .io, .tv, .co), and a site's TLD says nothing reliable about where it is hosted or who publishes it.
caveats.type: type describes how an entry is administered (sovereign_state, special_administrative_region, dependency, territory, uninhabited_area, contested_status); it is not a statement about sovereignty.
caveats.unStatus: unStatus is UN membership (member, observer_state, not_member), kept separate from ISO 3166-1 assignment.
caveats.relationships: relationship records an administrative arrangement and its kind; sovereigntyAsserted is always false. Contested cases carry a neutral note and no parent.
caveats.domains: Government/academic domain suffixes are listed only where the convention is well known; otherwise empty with provenance 'unknown'.
